clue.text: Constant fault if stove keeps hot

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one piece is put within the other
stove is a past tense of stave, to smash in, so the letters of fault if are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A faulty kitchen stove is described as a constant source of trouble when it holds its heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stove' looks like the cooker but is the anagram signal; FAULT IF rearranged gives FAITFUL, and 'keeps' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A constant friend or lover is a loyal, steadfast one, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Prominent female loves avoiding Republican

indicators.note: avoiding means doing without, so a letter is dropped from the love affairs

parts.note: amours are love affairs, so loves gives that word
R is the abbreviation for Republican in US politics

explanation.surface: A well-known woman keeps her romances clear of Republican men.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent person is widely known and celebrated, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Tension in spine distorted part of foot

indicators.note: in places the tension letter within the rearranged spine
distorted means bent out of shape, so the letters of spine are rearranged

parts.note: T is the physics symbol for tension

explanation.surface: Strain in a twisted backbone is blamed for warping part of the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' turns SPINE into INSEP, and 'in' sets T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched middle section of the upper foot, between toes and ankle, carries this name.

clue.text: It beats a red card

definitions.meaning: the organ that pumps blood beats, so it is the thing that beats
one of the two red suits in a deck gives its name to each card of that suit

explanation.surface: A card game where something trumps a red card.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ pulses in the chest, and the suit is one of the two red ones in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Working uniform, black clothing, European

parts.note: Uniform is the NATO radio alphabet word for U

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping round, so the black word dresses the European letter

parts.note: sable is the heraldic word for black

explanation.surface: A list of workwear: a uniform, black clothes, something from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' puts E inside SABLE, giving SEABLE after U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something working is in a state fit to be used, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: Casual traveller with lodging

indicators.note: lodging means housing someone, so the traveller word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a Rom is a Romani person, a traditional traveller
and means together with, so with gives that word

explanation.surface: A casual traveller turns up looking for a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: Rom, a Romani traveller, is a common crossword word; 'with' is a synonym here, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual and haphazard both describe what is done without plan or method.

clue.text: Musicians in first-class department gave up

indicators.note: in puts the musicians inside the first-class term

parts.note: A1, written A one, means first-class
a group of musicians is a band

explanation.surface: Players in a top department threw in the towel.
explanation.walkthrough: First-class is A1, which is spelt out in words as A plus the number one.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon something is to give it up or desert it, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Stop notice appearing in Democrat publication

indicators.note: appearing in places the notice inside the publication

parts.note: an issue of a magazine is a publication
an ad is a notice, as in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A notice is pulled from a Democratic party newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissuade someone is to talk them out of doing something, stopping them by argument.

clue.text: Opposed to appearing in web image for now

indicators.note: appearing in sets the opposition word within the web image

parts.note: a meme is an image or joke spread widely over the internet
anti means against or opposed to

explanation.surface: Someone objects to their picture being shown online, at least for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adverbially, as in 'meantime, wait here', it means for the present or in the interim.

clue.text: Note pale number that's wrong

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a pale is a pointed post, a stake

explanation.surface: A musical note, a pale and a number, one of which is incorrect.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mistaken is in error, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Outcome of a sharp turn in northern ocean?

definitions.text: Outcome of a sharp turn in northern ocean?

indicators.note: in puts the a-and-turn pair within the northern ocean

parts.note: the sea is the ocean
a U-turn is the sharpest turn, so it gives the letter U

explanation.surface: A ship swinging round hard in the North Sea leaves its passengers queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: violent turning in a rough northern sea brings on seasickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickness with an urge to vomit is what a lurching boat brings about in its passengers.

clue.text: Frail first of azaleas in gardens pulled up

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the upturned gardens
pulled up suits a down entry, so the gardens' name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Kew Gardens, in west London, is Britain's best-known botanic garden

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of azaleas

explanation.surface: A delicate first azalea is uprooted from the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is reversed to WEK and A goes in. KEW Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail and feeble both describe something lacking strength.

clue.text: As Oscar's quarry, supreme, not second-class

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the second-class letter

parts.note: something supreme cannot be bettered or beaten
B denotes second class, after A

explanation.surface: A supreme quarry, according to Oscar, is not second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde called fox-hunting 'the unspeakable in full pursuit of the uneatable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's description of the fox hunted by the gentry is a famous literary allusion.

clue.text: Distrust Dorothy hugging hubby only occasionally

indicators.note: hugging means holding close, so the name wraps round the chosen letters

parts.note: Dot is a short form of the name Dorothy

indicators.note: only occasionally takes every other letter of hubby, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Dorothy rarely embraces her husband, a sign of mistrust.
explanation.definitionFit: Distrust and the answer both mean a lack of confidence or belief in someone.

clue.text: Additional victim of Elizabeth's father

definitions.meaning: Sir Thomas, the Lord Chancellor beheaded in 1535 on the orders of Henry VIII, father of Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: Another person executed by the Tudor king.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra in amount is one sense; the other is the statesman and author of Utopia executed by Henry VIII.

clue.text: Medal enclosed in cube for submission

parts.note: the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the cube word

parts.note: a die is a small cube used in games
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosed, as on a letter

explanation.surface: A medal sealed in a box is handed over as a submission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosed' looks like the containment signal but is ENC, the letter-writer's abbreviation; 'in' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Submission and obedience both mean yielding to the will or orders of another.

clue.text: Taxonomic group making do, mainly preserved

indicators.note: preserved means kept inside, so the answer sits within the words making do mainly

explanation.surface: A biologist explains how a group of organisms mostly survived by managing with little.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological classification it is the top rank, such as animals or plants.

clue.text: Drew took off, nicking ring

indicators.note: nicking suggests getting in, so the ring word goes inside the mimic word

parts.note: to take off someone is to mimic them, so took off means aped
a peal is a ring of bells

explanation.surface: A thief takes off after pinching a ring, but the match was a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drew' is the past tense of draw in the sense of attracted.
explanation.definitionFit: If something appealed to you, it drew or attracted you.

clue.text: Just duke and earl waited

parts.note: to wait at table is to serve, so waited means served

explanation.surface: Only a duke and an earl stayed on to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only' but means fair or merited.
explanation.definitionFit: A just punishment is a merited one, earned by what was done.

clue.text: Affect priest related to nurse

parts.note: re means concerning or related to
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: A priest is moved by a nurse who is a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affect' here means to feign, not to influence.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect an accent is to put it on, to feign or fake it.

clue.text: Challenge bunch of desperadoes heading north

indicators.note: heading north suits a down entry, so the letters read upwards
a bunch of means a group of letters taken from within desperadoes

explanation.surface: A gang of outlaws riding north presents a challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunch of' takes ERAD from inside desperadoes and 'heading north' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dare is a challenge to do something risky, so the nouns match.

clue.text: Organisation's overdraft appears in Times

definitions.note: the clue's 's stands for is, linking definition to wordplay, so the definition is the noun organisation

indicators.note: appears in puts the overdraft letters inside the times word

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in three by four
OD is the banking abbreviation for overdrawn or overdraft

explanation.surface: A company's overdraft is reported in The Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An organisation such as a governing body or society is a corporate group of people.

clue.text: British artists impress very snooty virtuoso

indicators.note: impress means to stamp into, so very and snooty are pressed inside the artists

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, so two artists give the letters twice
U means upper-class, the word for a snooty or posh manner

explanation.surface: British painters are wowed by a showy, snobbish virtuoso.
explanation.walkthrough: U as a label for upper-class usage is a British convention from the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: A bravura performance is a virtuoso display of brilliance and skill.

clue.text: Unconvincing complaint about Nancy's article

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the complaint word reads backwards

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
Nancy is a French city, and le is a French definite article

explanation.surface: Someone makes a weak complaint about a newspaper piece on Nancy.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeble excuse is a weak, unconvincing one.

clue.text: Soft, easily digested pickle

parts.note: p is the music abbreviation for piano, meaning soft
a light meal is one that is easily digested

explanation.surface: A mild, easily digested pickle on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' looks like a food in this light meal but means a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a pickle means being in a difficult situation or predicament.

clue.text: Resin from tree around eastern India

indicators.note: around means the tree word goes round the eastern letter

parts.note: the elm is a common tree
India is the NATO radio alphabet word for I

explanation.surface: Resin collected from a tree in eastern India.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a fragrant gum resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and ointments.

clue.text: Bring up list limiting women's part of cycle

indicators.note: limiting means bounding on each side, so the rearing and listing words hold the women's letter between them

parts.note: to rear children is to bring them up
a ship that lists heels over to one side
W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

explanation.surface: Raise a list of limits on women's role in some cycle of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycle' looks like a sequence but is a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The back one of a bicycle's two wheels is a component of the machine.

clue.text: She was victorious over core of armada

indicators.note: over means covering, so the victory word goes round the core letters

parts.note: won means was victorious

indicators.note: core of takes the middle letters of armada

explanation.surface: A queen defeating the heart of the Spanish Armada.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Elizabeth I's victory over the Armada in 1588.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the pronoun used for a female person, so it stands for one.

clue.text: Fond diary describing Bordeaux, say

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, as in describing a circle, so the diary goes around the wine

parts.note: a log is a diary or record
Bordeaux is an example of a French wine, vin in French

explanation.surface: A sentimental diary recounts trips to the Bordeaux region.
explanation.definitionFit: A fond look is an affectionate one, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: It upsets my bum and gut

definitions.text: It upsets my bum and gut

indicators.note: upsets means throws into disorder, so the letters of my bum and gut are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone complains of something that disturbs their bottom and their stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer, since such an ailment does upset bowel and stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A stomach infection disturbs the digestive system at both ends, as the clue rudely says.

clue.text: Queen's favourite town in West Midlands

definitions.meaning: Robert, Earl of Leicester, was the favourite of Queen Elizabeth I
a town in the Black Country near Birmingham

explanation.surface: The monarch's favourite town in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert, Earl of Leicester, carried this surname; it is also a large Black Country town near Birmingham.

clue.text: Least obvious lover accepting one check

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the lover word holds the one letter

parts.note: a fan is a lover or devotee of something
I is the Roman numeral one
a test is a check

explanation.surface: A lover who accepts a single check makes the slightest impression.
explanation.definitionFit: The faintest trace is the weakest, least noticeable one, a superlative synonym.
